subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on theories of clinical depression, then mark my answer against the OCR spec.
promptWeak: Explain the dopamine hypothesis of schizophrenia for GCSE OCR Psychology simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: The OCR idea that mental health lies on a scale from healthy to unwell, and can change over time, is called the:
questions.explain: The mental health continuum describes mental health as a scale rather than a fixed 'ill or well' category, and it can shift over time.

questions.q: Which statement best reflects how attitudes to mental health in the UK have changed since the 1959 Mental Health Act?
options: Mental health problems are now hidden more than before
Care has moved entirely into institutions
There is generally more openness and reduced (though not removed) stigma
questions.explain: Since 1959 attitudes have generally become more open and accepting, and care has moved towards care in the community, though stigma remains.

questions.q: 'Prevalence' of a mental health problem refers to:
options: How many people have the condition in a population at a given time
questions.explain: Prevalence is the proportion of people in a population who have the condition; the spec also looks at differences by age, gender and sexual orientation.

questions.q: A negative label or mark of disgrace attached to people with a mental health problem is known as:
questions.explain: Stigma is negative labelling; the spec covers its effects on the individual both before and after diagnosis.

questions.q: An employer refuses to hire someone once they learn of the person's diagnosis. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Acting unfairly against someone because of their condition is discrimination, one of the effects the spec examines on individuals and wider society.

questions.q: Which is described as an effect of mental health problems on wider society in the OCR spec?
questions.explain: The spec lists effects on wider society, including care in the community as a way society responds to significant mental health problems.

questions.q: Clinical characteristics of schizophrenia in the OCR spec are drawn from which classification system?
questions.explain: The spec uses the clinical characteristics of schizophrenia and depression as outlined in the ICD (International Classification of Diseases).

questions.q: A person experiences hallucinations and delusions and shows disorganised thinking. These are characteristics of:
questions.explain: Hallucinations, delusions and disorganised thought are characteristic symptoms of schizophrenia as classified in the ICD.

questions.q: The biological theory of schizophrenia in the OCR spec proposes that symptoms are linked to:
questions.explain: The dopamine hypothesis suggests schizophrenia is linked to an overactive dopamine system and dysfunction in brain areas such as the frontal lobes and hippocampus.

questions.q: A key criticism raised against the dopamine hypothesis in the spec relates to which debate?
questions.explain: The dopamine hypothesis is criticised via the nature/nurture debate, as it emphasises biology over environmental and social factors.

questions.q: The psychological theory of schizophrenia in the OCR spec is the:
questions.explain: Social drift theory explains schizophrenia through rejection by society and disengagement, causing people to drift down the social scale.

questions.q: A criticism of social drift theory highlighted in the spec is the difficulty in establishing:
questions.explain: Social drift theory struggles to establish cause and effect: does social decline cause schizophrenia, or does schizophrenia cause the decline?

questions.q: Which is a recognised clinical characteristic of clinical depression?
options: Persistent low mood and loss of interest
questions.explain: Persistent low mood and loss of interest or pleasure are core ICD characteristics of clinical depression.

questions.q: The biological (evolutionary) theory of depression in the OCR spec is the:
questions.explain: Social rank theory sees depression as having an evolutionary function, with lower rank reducing conflict after a 'defeat'.

questions.q: Social rank theory is criticised in the spec mainly through which debate?
questions.explain: Social rank theory is criticised via the reductionism/holism debate, as reducing depression to an evolutionary rank mechanism may oversimplify it.

questions.q: In the ABC model of depression, what do the letters A, B and C stand for?
questions.explain: The ABC model: an Activating event triggers Beliefs (rational or irrational) which lead to emotional Consequences; irrational beliefs drive depression.

questions.q: After failing one test, a student thinks 'I always fail everything and I'm worthless.' In the ABC model this is an example of:
questions.explain: Over-generalising from one failure to total worthlessness is an irrational belief, which the ABC model links to depression.

questions.q: Which pair of drug treatments does the OCR spec link to schizophrenia and depression respectively?
questions.explain: The spec covers anti-psychotics (schizophrenia) and anti-depressants (depression), which change brain actions at the neuron/synapse level.

questions.q: The OCR core study Daniel, Weinberger et al. (1991) investigated schizophrenia by measuring:
options: Regional cerebral blood flow during cognitive activation
questions.explain: Daniel et al. (1991) studied the effect of amphetamine on regional cerebral blood flow during a cognitive task in people with schizophrenia.

questions.q: The OCR core study Tandoc et al. (2015) suggested that Facebook use was linked to depression mainly through:
questions.explain: Tandoc et al. (2015) found Facebook use predicted depression indirectly via envy: comparing yourself to others' posts can trigger envy, which links to depression.
